en:
"What's wrong? Are you feeling sick?"
...Someone had spoken to me, and I looked around.{p}

I was in an exam hall.
Oh, that's right.
I'd come to take the entrance exam for this high school.
"Your answer sheet's completely blank, isn't it?
There are only ten minutes left."
It was a familiar voice.
I knew that man's name.{p}

...Sadao Hino.
"You were the exam proctor?"
"Huh?
Oh, well, yeah, I am.
Hey, are you all right?
If you're feeling sick, I'll take you to the nurse's office.
You'd have to give up on the exam, though."
"...I'm fine."
I put a hand to my heavy head.
What on earth had I been seeing all this time?{p}

A dream?
No, it couldn't have been just a dream.
I was certain of it.
I would definitely get into this high school.
And then I would go to school here, and the man in front of me would ask me to do a feature on the school's seven wonders.
I even knew who was going to come.
Makoto Shindo, Nozomu Kazama, Shoji Arai, Tomoharu Hosoda, Akemi Iwashita, Reiko Fukuzawa.
And then...
No, maybe someone completely different would come.
"Five minutes left."
Hino announced it to everyone.{p}

Five minutes left.
That's right, I have to write my answers.
Answers?
There are no answers.
What answer could there possibly be in this school?{p}

...When I looked down at my desk, there was a textbook on it.
I was sure no one but me could see it.
No one was making a fuss, after all.
Even Hino hadn't said a thing.{p}

Or was he the one who put it there?
Did he know everything when he became the proctor?{p}

"That was amazing. You solved the whole thing in no time in the last five minutes."
After collecting the answer sheets, he came over to me.
...How phony.
As if he didn't know.
"I'm Hino, by the way.
I'm in the newspaper club.
Come find me if you get in.
If someone like you joined our club..."
"Sure."
"I'm counting on you.
Oh, right, what's your name?"
"It's {b} {a}."{p}

Hino went out into the hallway.
The proctor changed with each subject.
The next one was someone I had never seen before.
I filled in the answer sheet for each subject early, and spent the rest of the time thinking about them.
Them.
Yes, the ones who had spent that seven wonders meeting with me...{p}

...The exam was over.
What should I do?
Should I go straight home?{p}Or...
Go to the newspaper club room
Go to the old school building
Go home

I'll go to the newspaper club room.
I'm going to be relying on Hino for all sorts of things from now on.
It's better to say hello early.
I already know where the club room is, after all.
I walked down the hallway of the new school building.
I remembered walking down this hallway to cover the seven wonders.
It had been a dull, overcast evening, just like this one.
...Back then I'd been so anxious I couldn't stand it, but...{p}

"I've been waiting for you."
Just as I thought, he was there.
"I'm joining the newspaper club."
"Right. I figured you would."
He wasn't the least bit surprised.
Somehow his whole air seemed different.
Had the kind proctor he played been nothing but an act?{p}

"Who was it that called me here?"
"Called you?
Don't talk nonsense.
You chose to come here yourself."
"I... chose...?"
"You came here alone.
You took part in the seven wonders meeting alone, too.
All of it was what you wanted."
"Why would you say that?
You're the one who told me to cover the seven wonders, Hino."
"If you didn't like it, you could have quit.
You didn't have to listen to the seven wonders to the end, either.
You listened to the end.
And... you met him."{p}

"You mean Kawahara, don't you?"
"Don't go thinking it was fate.
You chose to come here yourself."
"...Was that really for the best, for him?"
"That's for Kawahara to decide."
"What... what should I do from now on?"
"Decide that yourself."
"All right.
I'll join the newspaper club.
That's my answer."
"That isn't an answer.
There are no answers.
You were thinking that yourself during the exam, weren't you?"
"Was I thinking something like that?"
"Want me to do an impression?"
"Please."{p}

"That's right, I have to write my answers.
Answers?
There are no answers.
What answer could there possibly be in this school?"
"...I understand.
There are no answers."
"You don't understand.
You don't understand a thing."
"I understand.
I don't understand a thing."
"That's right.
That's why you come here, isn't it?"
"Here...?"{p}

Hino slowly faded away.
I don't understand a thing.
That's why I come here.
Where is "here"?
The newspaper club?
Or the school?
Or maybe...{p}
As I was about to leave the club room, I bumped into someone.{p}

"Whoa, sor... oh, {a}?"
It was the proctor from earlier.
He had Hino's face, but this wasn't the real him.
"What, you came by the club room?
Thanks.
I hope you pass."
He was wearing the mask of a kind person again.
"I'll pass for sure."
"That's reassuring."
I asked Hino a question.
"Um, can I ask you one thing?"
"What?"
"I don't understand a thing.
When that happens, where is a person supposed to go?"{p}

Suddenly, a nasty smile spread across his face.
"What is it?"
He didn't reply.
He started walking away in silence.
...I see.
He doesn't understand either.
I started walking in the opposite direction from him.{p}

"Let's meet again, shall we?"
From somewhere, I heard Iwashita's voice.{p}

"I've found my answer.
I am who I am.
That's my answer."
Arai...
"{a}, if you're ever unsure what to do, you should talk it over with a friend.
If you'll have me, I'll be there for you."
That's Hosoda.{p}

"What are you talking about? That's ridiculous.
Thinking forever about stuff you can't figure out is a waste of time."
"Yeah, yeah, let's just have fun."
Kazama, and then Fukuzawa...{p}
"{a}, we're always right here."{p}

Where is "here"...?
Nursing my aching head, I started walking toward the exit.{p}
I'll go take a look at the old school building.{p}

"That building is off-limits, you know."
A familiar voice.
The one behind me had to be Arai.
"Yes... I know."
That was all I answered, and I started to go inside.
"Do you intend to go in?
You may not know this, but there are all sorts of rumors about that place."
I know.
About the old school building, and about you.
"Thank you for the warning."
That was all I said before I went inside.{p}
Footsteps followed me from behind.{p}

The hallway of the old school building was thick with the smell of old wood.
My nose was getting clogged with dust.{p}
...Suddenly, there was one more set of footsteps behind me.{p}

"Who are you?"
"Me?
Heh heh, does it matter who I am?"
"......"{p}
I climbed the stairs in front of me.{p}

"Why aren't you saying anything?"
Shindo...
The footsteps behind me grew in number, one by one.
They never once showed themselves in front of me.
Are we really walking together?{p}

When I reached the top of the stairs, I heard one more set of footsteps.
Someone was running up from behind.
"Huh? Who are you?"
It was Fukuzawa's voice.{p}
I kept walking.{p}
I passed the stairs and walked along the second-floor hallway.{p}

The footsteps behind me went on, just as before.
...Should I try turning around?{p}

Do the five behind me really come to this school every day?
I turned around without a word.{p}

The moment I did, the footsteps behind me stopped.
There was no one in front of me.
Had I only been hearing things...?
"Arai, you said you'd tell me about this school, didn't you?"
I murmured it to myself, alone.{p}

No, they must have told me already.
They told me all about the school, properly.
Though I feel as if I haven't heard enough yet.
......I'll enroll at this school, that's all.
And then I'll start it all again.
Scary Stories from School.
This alien space, this strange time.
Or perhaps, my fate.{p}

I'll go home.
I'm going to be attending this school, after all.
There'll be plenty of time to look around after that.
Today I'll get some good rest.{p}
......That night, I dreamed of the old school building.{p}

The old school building was being torn down.
It was crying, "It hurts, it hurts."
Or was it someone else who was crying?
"What's wrong?
Why are you crying?"
Someone spoke to me, and I woke up.{p}

"...Fukuzawa."
"{b}, too much has happened to you in such a short time.
You're going to get a good long sleep tonight, right?
That's fine, isn't it?
Let's sleep and not think about anything."
"During the exam, I was thinking about you and the others, Fukuzawa."
"That's right.
I knew.
But you don't have to think about us anymore."
"Why...?"
"This is a dream, right?
Whatever happens, it isn't real.
You don't have to think too hard.
You can even commit murder, or suicide.
And of course, you can sleep peacefully, too."{p}

Fukuzawa's hand softly touched my eyelids.
And I closed my eyes once more.{p}

...Cold drops fell onto my cheek from above.
"Sorry, it's nothing..."
Was it Fukuzawa who'd been crying?
The drops didn't stop.
Drip, drip, one drop after another fell onto my cheeks.
It was like looking up at the sky on a rainy day.
...I sensed many people at my side.
Are they all crying?
Is Kawahara here too?
Tonight, I'll sleep...{p}

Once again, I began to dream of the old school building crying.
Torn down by many people's hands, it was losing its shape.
Is a person's death like this, too?
What becomes of it once the shape is gone?
That's right, I'll think about it again when I wake up.
If I think about it every day, I'll understand someday.
I fell into a deep sleep.{p}
